claim: Vice President JD Vance presided over a series of meetings in the White House Situation Room in the summer of 2025 to manage the political fallout from the Jeffrey Epstein files, according to a New York Times report published in June 2026. The Times identified participants including White House chief of staff Susie Wiles, White House counsel David Warrington, press secretary Karoline Leavitt, communications director Steven Cheung, and Deputy Attorney General Todd Blanche, with former Attorney General Pam Bondi and FBI Director Kash Patel joining by phone; the report portrayed Vance as pressing to release the Justice Department's files even at the risk of damaging President Trump. Trump dismissed the account, calling it "total bullshit" and a Democratic diversion. On June 11, 2026, Representative Robert Garcia, the ranking Democrat on the House Oversight Committee, formally asked Chairman James Comer to call nine administration officials to testify about the handling of the Epstein files — Vance, chief of staff Susie Wiles, deputy chiefs of staff Tyler Budowich and James Blair, press secretary Karoline Leavitt, communications director Steven Cheung, FBI Director Kash Patel, former FBI deputy director Dan Bongino, and Associate Attorney General Stanley Woodward Jr. — and said any such testimony should be under oath and filmed. Because the minority lacks subpoena power, whether the committee compels testimony rests with Comer.

notes: Added after the meetings were dismissed too quickly on first pass. The Situation Room meetings are real and reported by the NYT (June 2026), corroborated across The Hill, Daily Beast, Yahoo, and Raw Story, and not denied by the White House — Trump disputed the framing, not the fact of the meetings. NYT is uncrawlable from this environment (cited url:null, verified via secondaries). What is verified is the existence of the meetings and who attended; the reel's characterization that they were held 'to protect Trump' is the contested part — the NYT account actually portrayed Vance as wanting to release the files even if it hurt Trump, which cuts against a simple shield-Trump reading. Attribute, don't adopt: the meetings happened (recorded here); the coverup-purpose inference is the editorial proposition. Anchor y2019 (Epstein cluster); year=2025 marks when the meetings occurred.
